headline: Reptiles let the environment control their temperature—a strategy that's worked for 300 million years
universal_truth: Efficiency often beats power; using less can be an advantage
fun_facts: Cold-blooded animals need only 10% of the food that warm-blooded animals of the same size require
Some reptiles can survive for months without eating
Crocodiles have remained virtually unchanged for 80 million years—older than T. rex
discussion_questions: What are the advantages of being cold-blooded?
Why didn't reptiles evolve warm blood like mammals?
What limits where cold-blooded animals can live?

hook.script: Reptiles don't waste energy heating themselves—they let the sun do it. This seems primitive, but it's actually efficient. Cold-blooded animals need only 10% of the food mammals need. For 300 million years, this strategy has worked brilliantly.

cliff.script: We call it 'cold-blooded' as if it's inferior. But reptiles have thrived for hundreds of millions of years. What advantages does letting the environment control your temperature provide?
cliff.prompt: What's the advantage of being cold-blooded?

options.text: Massive energy savings—no need to eat constantly to maintain body temperature
options.response: Yes. You can survive on far less food, go months without eating, and live in places where food is scarce. Efficiency is a superpower.

options.text: Cold-blooded animals can live in more extreme temperatures
options.response: Actually, they're limited to moderate climates. The advantage is energy efficiency...

fact1.title: Energy Efficiency
fact1.script: Mammals burn 90% of their food just to stay warm. Reptiles use almost all their food for growth and activity. A crocodile can survive a year on what a lion eats in a week. Less input, comparable output.

fact2.title: Ancient Design
fact2.script: Crocodiles have barely changed in 80 million years—they watched dinosaurs come and go. Their design works so well that evolution hasn't needed to improve it. Stability is its own form of success.

fact3.title: Trade-offs
fact3.script: Cold-blooded animals are limited by climate—they can't survive where it's too cold. They're sluggish until warmed up. But in warm environments, they're incredibly successful. Every strategy has trade-offs.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Efficiency often beats power. Reptiles teach that using less can be an advantage. Not every problem requires more energy—sometimes the answer is needing less.

outro.script: That's Day 141. Tomorrow, we'll explore animals living in two worlds—amphibians. Until then, appreciate the efficient design of creatures that let their environment do the work.

growTrack.title: Efficiency Thinking - Do More With Less
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply efficiency thinking to life situations
growTrack.activity: Identify one area of your life where you could 'go cold-blooded'—achieving the same result with less energy, less effort, or fewer resources. Sometimes the best solution isn't doing more, but needing less.
